record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can practitioners perform what-if analysis by modeling changes in an underlying networking system and then generating synthetic data for the modified system, especially when larger interventions invalidate the conditional distributions learned from the original data and may therefore require explicit physical-system modeling or simulation?

evidence.quote: Another direction of interest is to enable 'what-if' analysis, in which practitioners can model changes in the underlying system and generate associated data.
Such what-if analysis is likely to require physical system modeling/simulation, while GANs may be able to help model individual agent behavior.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a networked system that produces multivariate time series data, where each trace records the temporal behavior of agents (e.g., flows, users, devices) interacting through shared infrastructure. Suppose a generative model G (such as a GAN) has been trained on observed traces drawn from a joint distribution P(X, C), where X denotes the time series and C denotes auxiliary system parameters or conditions (e.g., topology, link capacities, traffic mix, protocol settings). Standard conditional generation can produce samples X ~ G(· | C) for values of C represented in the training data.

Now suppose a practitioner wishes to perform "what-if" analysis: predict and synthesize plausible time series for a modified system specified by a new condition C' that represents an intervention (for example, changing routing, introducing a new protocol, scaling the user population, or altering link capacities). When the intervention is small, one might hope that the learned conditional distribution P(X | C) extrapolates to C'; however, when the intervention is large, the original conditional distributions become invalid because the underlying physical/networking dynamics are themselves altered.

Formulate and solve the following problem:

(a) Provide a principled framework that combines a learned generative model of agent-level or fine-grained behavior with an explicit mechanistic / physical-system simulator of the network so that, given an intervention C' outside the training distribution, the framework produces synthetic time series whose joint distribution faithfully approximates the true post-intervention distribution P*(X | do(C')).

(b) Specify identifiability conditions on the decomposition (which aspects of behavior are modeled by G versus by the simulator) under which the resulting hybrid generator is consistent as the amount of pre-intervention training data grows.

(c) Develop quantitative evaluation criteria — beyond marginal or conditional fidelity on observed C — for assessing the accuracy of synthetic data produced under counterfactual interventions C', and demonstrate the framework on a concrete networked time-series setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning how to combine GAN-based generative modeling with physical/network simulation to support out-of-distribution counterfactual ("what-if") synthesis of networked time series. No published work has been identified that provides a complete, principled solution; subsequent literature on hybrid simulator-ML generators and causal time-series GANs addresses related sub-problems but does not resolve the full question.

status_evidence.title: DoppelGANger and follow-ups
status_evidence.snippet: Repository for the DoppelGANger framework for generating networked time-series; documentation lists what-if/counterfactual generation as a noted limitation/open direction.
status_evidence.claim: Counterfactual/what-if synthesis under large system interventions is described as an open direction rather than a solved capability.
